title: Scaling the Ray Serve Controller to Thousands of Replicas | Anyscale | Ray Summit 2026

Abra Shik. I work on the race serve

process within the race serve cluster

brain of the surf cluster. In the past
one year we identified some performance
bottleneck in in the serve controller.
And uh today we'll talk about how we

Uh before we get started I want to set
the stage about like where we are

ser cluster could get to is about
thousand and beyond that the cluster

as of today with the latest build of
racefer
cluster can get up to like 4,000

decisions it's able to make by 9x

secondond introduction to rayerf. Um

uh topology looks like. uh and and

plane of surf uh array surf cluster. At

then finally broadcasts routing tables

surf controller is what typic is is what
we typically refer to as a control plane
of surf cluster.
In today's presentation, I'll walk
through exactly how the surf controller

it, our experimentation setup that

Surf controller is a single Python

node. It has a single async.io event

Um node update is responsible for
bookkeeping and tracking all the nodes
in the cluster. Deployment state handles

everything from starting a start
starting a replica stopping a replica to

managing the ingress points in the

that h that regularly happen as part of
the reconciliation loop within uh race

from handles and replicas are
communicated to the surf controller.
uh status endpoints, dashboard queries
all land up on the same event loop that
uh manages all like all the other
operations we talked about. Um every
time a user sends a request to deploy a
application or change a config within
surf cluster uh those are also handled
by surf controller. And finally, all the
routing table broadcasts are is also
something um serve controller manages
internally and communicates that to the
rest of the cluster. If we were to
imagine this in a timeline, since surf
controller is a reconciliation loop that
infinitely runs, um it does uh two key
piece uh like it does two operations.
One is a set of blocking operations uh
which involves the four things we
discussed before. and then for it it it
uh it does a non-blocking sleep of 100
milliseconds. So the reason why I
mentioned this is because when the
blocking operations are being executed
um none of the RPCs from the cluster are
getting executed. The only opportunity
the RPCs have uh is during the the 100
millisecond async sleep. Um so it's
highly important that the core cluster
uh controller operations are efficient
and also the RPCs are efficient because
e if either one of them u blocks the
event loop for uh reasonably long amount
of time it impacts the performance of
the other.
The other important detail to note here
is um the autoscaling decision made in
nth control loop step is applied to the
cluster in in n +1 step. So if the RPCs
are blocking the event loop for long
enough, that has a direct correlation to
how lagged the autoscaling behavior is
in the cluster. Um, and the reason we
care about quick autoscaling decision is
because the longer the autoscaler takes
to make a decision, um, the slower the
reaction time is going to be, which
means the longer the user request sits

uh, request latencies.
Um so what we noticed was in in

This went unnoticed but over a period of

path to optimize the controller

In order to accurately benchmark serve
controllers performance we uh we built
this sample app. It contains two
deployments. One called metric
generator. The other one is called hello
world. Um the metrics generator
deployment is the one that's allowed to
autoscale from 100 to 2,000 replicas

measuring the performance. Each [snorts]

behavior in order to measure the
autoscaling uh in order to measure the
performance of surf controller
accurately. Um so the reason why this
app is uh u like noteworthy is because
this setup allows us to maximally
saturate the controller's event loop

autoscaling metric to the controller but
at the same time the handle that's
holding reference to the downstream

Um, so we take that app, we sweep
through some predefined set of replica

uh measure the controller's performance

results. More notably, we um we captured
three important metrics. One is amount

Um what's evident from the baseline
benchmark is that at about thousand

acceptable but beyond that uh the

So here here are series of optimizations
we applied that allowed us to achieve
that 4x scale. Um the first thing we did
was migrate from pedantic v1 to pedantic
2 not just in rayer but across the
entire ray library. Um this gave us a
free performance improvement because
pant because uh for the reason that
pedantic 2 2's object validation is
implemented in uh pure rust uh and they
migrated away from like native python
that naturally improved the runtime
performance of pedantic objects serve
internally uses pedantic quite heavily
to represent the state of the cluster.
Just to give you an example, every
replica in the race of cluster is
represented as one pedantic data model
object in the controller. So uh we do a
lot of object creation and we run many
object validations. So it's it's it was
important for us to like improve the
performance of those operations. Um and
we got all of that for free just by
migrating to V2. As part of the
migration, we noticed some antiatterns
of how we were using pedantic like in
this example um in like before migration
or before optimization as you can see um
we used to have a reference to pedantic
model. We used to des serialize it or
sorry serialize it into a python object
then mutate that python dictionary and
then recreate the the the pedantic
object. uh this operation is extremely
expensive because one creation of the
object um and the second reason is every
time we create the object padantic used
to rerun all the validations. Um but in
fact we could have been a bit more
clever here just by using the model copy
API which uh mutates the object in place
and then skips the validation. Um we can
afford to skip validation here uh for
the reason that um the data that we are
mutating the object with is fully
controlled by the framework. So we can
make safe judgment calls that those
attributes are safe. Um this change uh
this uh single line of change improved
the the cost of this operation dropped
the cost of this operation from 83
millisecond to 11 millisecond. So about
uh 8x improvement in performance.
Next I'm going to talk about how we
optimized a part of the autoscaler
algorithm in reserve. Um
in the way the autoscaler works is the
surf controller computes the total
number of ongoing requests in the surf
cluster, compares that with a target
number of ongoing requests that is set
by the user and then the relative delta
between those two is what determines the
uh whether the cluster should upscale or
downscale. Right? But the key here is
figuring out the total number of ongoing
requests in the entire cluster. Right?
So the way uh that works is as follows.
Every replica in the cluster is emitting
um a time series data which represents
the total number of ongoing requests on
that replica and every handle um is is
emitting a set of time series data one
corresponding to each replica it's
responsible for. Um and all those time
series
uh data uh enter surf controller. surf
controller runs a kway merge algorithm
across those time series to to compose
them into like one time series and then
uh it's a sum operation across across
all the like end time series and then we
run a backward average on that uh on
that single time series. So uh this
approach is highly accurate in terms of
computing the total number of ongoing
requests but uh the pure algorithm is
implemented in Python and it was really
expensive. We swapped that out with a
Syon implementation that significantly
improved the performance of this
algorithm. Uh the latencies here dropped
from 24 milliseconds to 2 milliseconds.
So about 13x improvement.
Next I'm going to talk about how we
optimize the metrics injection path in
surf controller. As I mentioned before
all the replicas and handles are
constantly emitting these autoscaling
metric objects to surf controller.
Replicas are emitting a single time
series data whereas the handles are
reporting a set of time series data.
Right? the objects from the handles are
considerably uh larger in size just
because every handle is responsible for
numerous replicas on the cluster. So the
size of the object can get as large as
70 to 80 kilobytes. Um so there are two
problems here. One is transferring large
objects over the wire through RPCs are
relatively expensive. And then in the
old implementation we used Python's
cloud pickle library to serialize at the
source and then des serialize at the
destination. And that uh the usage of
cloud pickle itself is also uh expensive
since it's all implemented in native
Python.
We changed that out. We we changed the
serialization protocol to use uh zlib
instead which did compression at the
source and decompression at the
destination. that solved the large
payload be being transferred over the
wire problem and also the serialization
and deserialization cost uh
substantially dropped. The second uh
change we made the the second
optimization we changed to this metrics
flow is to throttle RPC calls at the
source which means if a if a RPC request
is already in flight we stop sending any
more data until the previous one
completes which was not the case before.
we were sending RPCs unconditionally. So
uh um RPC requests used to get cued in
the controllers asyncio event loop which
is not good. Um so before the
optimization so this is a flame graph of
CPU utilization from the serve
controller process as you can see
significant amount of CPU time is being
spent in d serializing the RPC requests
and post optimization
uh the flame graphs look significantly
better a lot of idle CPUs to do other to
like to do other things on surf
controller
here is another view of that
optimization. There are two plots here.

The x-axis is amount of time the
controller is allowed to run and yaxis
is metrics injection delay uh which
which basically is measuring the amount
of time taken for the uh the the metric
RPC to travel from replica to the
controller. In the pre-optimization

uh snowball and balloon over time and
constantly increase and gets as high as

The choice of compression
um algorithm was between Zlib and

uh for two reason. One uh is because

Ray library which was not um

The last optimization I want to talk
about is how we improved the health
check mechanism in race controller. Uh
one of the important responsibilities of
surf controller is to constantly health
check all the replicas in the cluster
and if there are any replicas that are
unhealthy we take it out of rotation and
then reinstate a new replica like in its
place. Uh hence guaranteeing like
availability overall.
Uh
but in order to do that historically
serve controller used to scan like if
the cluster contains thousand replicas
controller used to loop over all
thousand replicas in every controller
tick. Um this is a little bit wasteful
because
the the health check timeout set by the
user on a replica is 10 seconds. So we
only care about actually doing the
health check RPCs every 10 seconds. So
looping over all replicas even if we are
not doing the actual RPC was a little
bit uh wasteful when so when the
controller loops over each of these
replica it asks like three important
questions. It asks whether is a health
check due now if yes we start an RPC. If
an RPC is already in flight, then we try
to pull the result of that uh of that
request. And finally, if previous three
requests resulted in a failure, then we
conclude that the replica is unhealthy,
we we we kill the actor and recreate a
new one.
So even though we're not making RPCs in
every controller tick, just the act of

changed this model from looping over all
replicas to looping over a subset of

set. So in every controller tick we

consider those two. In addition we all
we always
um include the replicas that are marked
for migration and the replicas that are
already that already have an ongoing
health check into the set. The size of
the window can be controlled through an

uh that factor takes a value between 0

the window is smaller value means larger
window uh and larger factor value like
uh results in a smaller window size um
the choice the the width of the window

neat tradeoff, right? Uh if we consider
a large set of replicas in every

check overall, but we compromise on the
